chart.title: Used to — past habits

intro_examples.text: I used to play video games inside.
intro_examples.continuation: Now I play outside every day.

intro_examples.text: My friend didn't use to have a computer.

rows: I used to play video games inside.
She used to have long hair.
Children used to learn without computers.
My friend didn't use to have a computer.
Yes, I did. / No, I didn't.
chart.note_rule: Use 'used to' for past habits that don't happen now.
chart.note_exception: Question: Did + subject + use to + verb?
chart.note_exception_detail: 'Used to' is different from 'be used to'

rules.title: Positive — used to + verb
rules.subtitle: Use used to + verb to say something happened regularly in the past but doesn't happen now.

transforms.to: She used to have long hair

examples.text: I used to play outside every day.
examples.jp: 毎日外で遊んでいました。

examples.text: She used to have a pet rabbit.
examples.jp: 彼女はペットのウサギを飼っていました。

rules.title: Negative — didn't use to + verb
rules.subtitle: Use didn't use to + verb to say something did NOT happen regularly in the past.

transforms.to: People didn't use to have computers
People didn't use to have cell phones

examples.jp: 昔、人々は電気を持っていませんでした。

examples.text: My friend didn't use to like reading.
examples.jp: 友達は前は読書が好きではありませんでした。

rules.title: Question — Did + subject + use to + verb?
rules.subtitle: To ask about past habits, use Did + subject + use to + verb? Answer with Yes, I did or No, I didn't.

transforms.to: Did you use to walk to school?
Did people use to travel by horse?

explanation.title: Rule 2 — Negative form
explanation.body: The negative form is didn't use to + verb. The correct answer is didn't use to. Rule 2 We never say 'used to not' or 'not used to'.
